runtime_version: vllm==0.19.0 + transformers==5.4.0 (--no-deps pin on top of the base image, per D55)

inference_config.hash_weights_on_load_reason: 70.21 GB of safetensors; a full sha256 pass costs minutes of paid GPU idle per worker start. The largest file is verified against weights.largest_file_sha256 instead and the full manifest is produced once at image build time.

notes: LICENCE STATUS IS verified (founder decision 2026-09-03; receipts/registry-updates/license-infinity_parser2_pro.json). The checkpoint infly/Infinity-Parser2-Pro is Apache-2.0 on its model card and in benchmark/v6/candidate-registry.yaml; license.text_sha256 above is the sha256 of that model card's README.md fetched read-only from the pinned revision. This was never about the weights: the official runtime wrapper repository github.com/infly-ai/INF-MLLM still carries NO LICENSE file at its root and none under Infinity-Parser2/ (checked 2026-09-03 via the GitHub contents API; the repo's `license` field is null). Readable is not reusable: that code may be read but not copied, ported or vendored. The design-around is to use no INF-MLLM code at all.

DESIGN-AROUND: this runtime serves the checkpoint with the `vllm serve` command printed on the model card itself and calls it over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint with the model card's own prompt and sampling values. The `infinity_parser2` PyPI wrapper (version 0.4.0, built from the unlicensed repo) is deliberately NOT installed.

VRAM BASIS, measured not guessed: the HF blob listing for revision b27d4701 sums to 70,214,492,328 bytes of safetensors (70.21 GB) across 15 shards; the two largest shards are 32.42 GB each (Qwen3.5-MoE expert blocks). At bf16 that does not leave a usable KV cache on one 80 GB card at the model card's --max-model-len 65536, which is why the card itself prints --tensor-parallel-size 2. gpu_min_vram_gb 160 is therefore an AGGREGATE across two 80 GB devices, not a per-device figure. Masterplan 13.3 lists A100 80 / H100 for this lane and marks the canary mandatory; the canary decides whether TP=2 is required or whether a single 80 GB device with a reduced max_model_len is enough.

WEIGHTS_STRATEGY IS volume_cache AND runtime_mode_allowed IS ["baked", "bootstrap"] (founder decision 2026-09-03, superseding ARENA_CONTRACT D36's baked-only reversal of 2026-09-03 20:15). Baked-only was an operational choice about the stall risk, not a licence question, and the founder chose to keep bootstrap available: a bootstrap canary fetches the 70.21 GB of weights once into a persistent RunPod network volume rather than into pod-local ephemeral storage, and MUST pass the controller's `--volume-gb` flag so the weights are cached on the volume instead of re-downloaded on every pod start. Masterplan 15.1's stall-risk concern (a 70 GB boot download inside a metered pod) is addressed by the volume cache, not by forbidding bootstrap outright: the download happens once per volume, not once per pod. The baked path stays available and still bakes the checkpoint into /opt/arena/weights/infinity_parser2_pro at image build time; the canary decides which path this lane actually runs with.

Masterplan 47 H4 is the hypothesis this runtime exists to test: whether the published olmOCR-Bench 87.6 / ParseBench 74.3 reproduce on the campaign's pinned evaluators. Those figures are the vendor's own and are quoted, never claimed as reproduced.

The model card's Limitations section is part of the record: English and Chinese only, degraded on other languages, weaker on complex charts and rotated tables, does not capture bold/italic/strikethrough.

PROMPT KIND text (ARENA_CONTRACT D34). adapter.py sends AdapterConfig.prompt_text verbatim as the text part of the chat message and refuses an empty one; it carries no copy of the prompt. prompt_registry/infinity_parser2_pro_doc2json_v1.txt is therefore the only place the doc2json prompt bytes live, and its sha256 is what every receipt records.

Framework-floor audit (2026-09-03, after the GLM-OCR canary died on an unrecognised model_type): the required framework floor, what the pinned base image actually ships, the action taken and the evidence URLs are recorded in provenance.json under framework_floor_audit. bootstrap.sh asserts the pinned framework versions and that the framework recognises this checkpoint's architecture before anything starts.

D55 (2026-09-04): the 2026-09-03 audit above concluded the vllm==0.17.1-bundled Qwen3_5MoeConfig/Qwen3_5MoeTextConfig shim was enough and left transformers unpinned. Real canary pod gx5b5cakrhp359 (2xH100, 2026-09-04) proved that wrong: vLLM resolved the architecture fine and then died with `ValueError: Tokenizer class TokenizersBackend does not exist or is not currently imported` (transformers/models/auto/tokenization_auto.py via vllm/tokenizers/hf.py) -- the checkpoint's tokenizer_config.json declares tokenizer_class=TokenizersBackend (confirmed by fetching that file at revision b27d4701 from huggingface.co), a class that exists only in transformers v5.x (src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py), and vllm 0.17.1 bounds transformers to '>= 4.56.0, < 5' (requirements/common.txt), so the image's transformers 4.x never had that class at all -- the bundled vllm config shim was never in that code path. The fix follows the same family glm_ocr already proved on this exact image: base_image bumped to vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-ubuntu2404@sha256:69234fc3... (same digest glm_ocr pins, CUDA 12.9.1, min_cuda_version unchanged at 12.9) with transformers==5.4.0, tokenizers==0.22.2, huggingface_hub==1.5.0, hf-xet==1.3.2 installed --no-deps on top, exactly glm_ocr's pins. Verified: transformers v5.3.0 (the checkpoint's own declared transformers_version) already maps model_type qwen3_5_moe/qwen3_5_moe_text to Qwen3_5Tokenizer in CONFIG_MAPPING_NAMES/TOKENIZER_MAPPING_NAMES and transformers.tokenization_utils_tokenizers.TokenizersBackend is importable from v5.0 onward; vllm v0.19.0's model_executor/models/registry.py still registers Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration and vllm/transformers_utils/configs/qwen3_5_moe.py still carries Qwen3_5MoeConfig/Qwen3_5MoeTextConfig (model_type qwen3_5_moe_text), so the D33/2026-09-03 preflight's vLLM-side checks stay valid unchanged; a transformers-side check (CONFIG_MAPPING_NAMES + TokenizersBackend importability) was added ahead of it. bootstrap.sh's architecture preflight now runs BEFORE the 70.21 GB weight download (fetching only config.json + tokenizer_config.json via hf_hub_download for the check) rather than after, and bootstrap.sh now exports ARENA_WEIGHTS_DIR so entrypoint.sh reuses the directory bootstrap already resolved instead of resolving the same 70.21 GB checkpoint a second time (pod gx5b5cakrhp359 downloaded it twice: once into /workspace by bootstrap.sh, again into /opt by entrypoint.sh, because bootstrap.sh never exported the variable entrypoint.sh's default falls back to).
